summary: Richard Gombrich is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who earned his BA and DPhil at the University of Oxford, also studying under K. R. Norman, Walpola Rahula, and Gananath Obeyesekere. He served as Boden Professor at Oxford from 1965 to 2004.

Richard Hartshorne studied at Princeton University (~1916–1920) and the University of Chicago (~1920–1924). He held academic posts at the University of Minnesota (~1924–1940) and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1940–1970).

Richard Hauschild was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Tübingen, Leipzig, and Jena (PhD 1926, Habilitation 1948) under Albert Debrunner and Johannes Hertel. He held posts at the University of Jena from 1938 to 1967, including professor from 1951.

Richard Henebry was a linguist who studied at St. John's College, Waterford, St Patrick's Pontifical University, Maynooth, and the universities of Greifswald and Freiburg. He also studied under Heinrich Zimmer (~1896–1898).

Richard Hugh Robinson was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Alberta, SOAS, and London under Edward Conze, David Snellgrove, Arthur Waley, and David Friedman. He taught at Toronto and became a professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison.

Richard Hughes Seager works in religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Wisconsin System, Harvard Divinity School, and Harvard University (PhD), and was appointed Associate Professor of Religion at Hamilton College around 1994.

Philosopher Richard Hönigswald studied at the University of Graz, the University of Vienna (~1894–1902), and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1902–1904). He held posts at the University of Breslau (1906–1930) and the University of Munich (1930–1933).

Richard J. Davidson studied at New York University (BA 1972) and Harvard University (PhD 1976). He held key posts at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, serving as professor (from 1987), co-director (from 1996), and director (2001–2017).

Richard Jay Kohn was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1988, studying under doctoral supervisor Geshe Lhundup Sopa as well as Lama Tharchin Rinpoche.

Richard K. Payne is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who studied under Chisei Aratano and Taisen Miyata. He served as dean at the Institute of Buddhist Studies around 1995 and on the Graduate Theological Union doctoral faculty in 2016.

Linguist Richard Karl Heinrich von Kienle completed his Habilitation under Hermann Güntert at Heidelberg in 1934, later serving there as PD and professor. He was a professor at the University of Hamburg (1941–1946) and Free University of Berlin (1953–1974).

Richard Keith Sprigg was a scholar in linguistics and Tibetology who was educated at Oakham School. He held an academic post at the University of London and SOAS University of London from around 1948 to 1980.

Richard Kieckhefer is a historian and religious studies scholar who studied at Saint Louis University, MGH, and UT Austin (PhD 1972). He served as a professor at Northwestern University from 1975 and as president of Societas Magica and ASCH.

Richard King is a scholar of religious studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at Dalhousie, McGill, and Lancaster (PhD ~1992) under Daniel Mariau, and held posts at Stirling (~1993–2000), Vanderbilt (~2004–2011), and Glasgow (~2011).
Richard Kühnau was an Indologist who completed his PhD at the University of Breslau between 1878 and 1885, where he studied under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler and Alfred Hillebrandt.

Richard Lionel Spittel worked in Indology and medicine, earning an L.M.S. from Ceylon Medical College after attending Royal College, Colombo. He served as a lecturer at Ceylon Medical College and held a post at the National Hospital of Sri Lanka in 1910.

Richard Löbbecke was an Indologist who earned his PhD at Leipzig (1908) under Ernst Windisch, having also studied at Marburg, Göttingen, and Berlin under scholars including Kielhorn, Andreas, Pischel, Geldner, Sieg, Huth, Lindner, and Conrady.

Richard M. Jaffe works in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He held a post at North Carolina State University (~1995–1999) before serving as Professor of Religious Studies at Duke University from around 1999.

Richard Morris was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics who trained at Battersea Training College. He taught at King's College School (1869) and served as headmaster at the Royal Masonic School for Boys (1875–1888) and Dedham Grammar School (~1888–1894).

Richard O. Meisezahl, a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies, earned his PhD at the University of Bonn in 1944. He worked as an assistant there from 1945 to 1947 and founded the International Institute for Tibetan and Buddhist Studies.
